name: Joshua
description: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest

points: The sign shewed the people whose hand their life was in: Moses is the man to hearken to, so do not speak against him. And Joshua discomfited Amalek with the edge of the sword; Joshua was a mighty warrior even then.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Write this for a memorial in a book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: for I will utterly put out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven. Moses wrote it, and Deuteronomy 25 is that rehearsal: remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way.

note.label: Exodus 17: Water Out of the Rock and War With Amalek

points: His servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, departed not out of the tabernacle. Joshua was a true disciple, a learner, eager to stay by Moses' side and learn; the Lord knew his spirit.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes.

For they are bread for us. They said, they are food for us, we can take them by the power of the Lord. It said Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes, meaning they were furious and sorrowful for the false report that was given. So Joshua and Caleb did have a different kind of spirit on them, because they did not go with the general populace with their false report. How do you know not to go along with what a populace is saying when it is contrary to the Lord? The spirit of God must be upon you.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: The tenth provocation was the report of the spies, and it was the last: how long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun, because Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Among these numbered by Moses and Eleazar in the plains of Moab there was not a man of them that was numbered in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said of them, they shall surely die in the wilderness; and there was not left a man of them, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun.

Why Caleb and Joshua? They had another spirit on them and did not doubt when the Lord sent them to spy out the land. My servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land; he let nobody keep him from serving the Most High.

note.label: Numbers 26: The Second Census of the Families of Israel

points: And the Lord said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him. So Joshua also had the spirit, the Holy Spirit, upon him.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: The Lord answered: take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

points: Moses did as the Lord commanded him: he took Joshua, set him before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation, laid his hands upon him, and gave him a charge, as the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

points: The Lord named the men which shall divide the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, and one prince of every tribe, Caleb the son of Jephunneh for Judah and the rest by name.

note.label: Numbers 34: The Borders of the Land of Canaan

points: Joshua was commanded at that time: thine eyes have seen all that the Lord your God hath done unto these two kings; so shall he do unto all the kingdoms whither thou passest.
Ye shall not fear them, for the Lord your God he shall fight for you; the victories over Sihon and Og were the proof set before Joshua's own eyes.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: But charge Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him, for he shall go over before this people and cause them to inherit the land. The Most High said plainly whom he would deal with for the crossing.

note.label: Deuteronomy 3: The Battle Is the Lord's

points: The Most High himself goes over before Israel to destroy these nations, and Joshua goes over before the people, as he did to Sihon and Og, kings of the Amorites.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

points: Moses calls Joshua in the sight of all Israel and charges him: be strong and of a good courage, for thou must go with this people into the land sworn to their fathers, and cause them to inherit it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

points: The Most High tells Moses his days approach that he must die, and to call Joshua to the tabernacle to receive his charge; the Most High appears in the pillar of a cloud over the door of the tabernacle.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

points: Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him. Joshua was Moses' protege, and he carried the spirit Moses had, a great leader compassionate for the people; and the children of Israel hearkened unto him, and did as the Lord commanded Moses.

note.label: Deuteronomy 34: The Death of Moses

points: Joshua is called Moses' minister because when Moses was the leader, Joshua was the one always cleaving to him. He was not close to Moses in age; he was one of the young men that cleaved unto his elder, and if Moses was a good leader, beloved among the children of Israel, who better to rise up in his stead than the man who has his spirit?

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

points: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there. Because they were going to take the land.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there.

note.label: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies

points: So the two men returned, and descended from the mountain, and passed over, and came to Joshua the son of Nun, and told him all things that befell them: and they said unto Joshua, Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land. This is going to be easy, to kill everybody. For even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. That woman told them the reason why you are going to win is because everybody is afraid. And then she kept it a secret. She said, I am not going to tell them.

note.label: When God Reveals His Secrets!

points: They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised.

note.label: Joshua 2: Rahab and the Spies

points: Joshua rose early in the morning, and Israel removed from Shittim and came to Jordan and lodged there before passing over. After three days the officers went through the host to spread the orders and instructions the people had to abide by.

note.label: Joshua 3: Jordan Driven Back

points: The Lord told Joshua, this day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee. The people were about to see the Lord rocking with Joshua the same way he rocked with Moses.

note.label: Joshua 3: Jordan Driven Back

points: Joshua called Israel to hear the words of the Lord: hereby ye shall know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive out from before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.

note.label: Joshua 3: Jordan Driven Back

points: Joshua also set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan itself, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark stood, and they are there unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial

points: The priests which bare the ark stood in the midst of Jordan until every thing was finished that the Lord commanded Joshua to speak unto the people, and the people hasted and passed over.

note.label: Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial

points: On that day the Lord magnified Joshua in the sight of all Israel, and they feared him as they feared Moses all the days of his life. A man through whom the Lord makes a whole river stand up commands that reverence.

note.label: Joshua 4: The Twelve Stone Memorial

points: And those twelve stones, which they took out of Jordan, did Joshua pitch in Gilgal.

note.label: From Broken Men Comes Ungodly Generations

points: Circumcise again the children of Israel the second time: the children of Israel had not been keeping the commandments, being stiffnecked and hardheaded, and the Lord told Joshua to fix them.

When Abraham received the commandment he performed it, circumcising every male of his house the selfsame day; he showed the Lord by his actions that he believed. So the men in Joshua who had not been circumcised showed a form of repentance by applying the law of circumcision.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

points: Their children raised up in their stead Joshua circumcised, for they had not circumcised them by the way.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

points: Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand, and Joshua stepped to him: art thou for us, or for our adversaries?

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Joshua lifted up his eyes by Jericho and saw a man standing over against him with his sword drawn, a warrior. Joshua did not run; he went straight to him and asked, Art thou for us, or for our adversaries? There was no fear in the heart of Joshua.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

points: When Joshua realized who stood before him, the fear came: he fell on his face to the earth and did worship, and the leader of Israel's army called himself a servant, saying, What saith my lord unto his servant? Joshua had cleaved to Moses and understood who the captain of the host is.

The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

points: The captain of the Lord's host said, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy. And Joshua did so.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

points: The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.

note.label: Joshua 6: The Fall of Jericho and the Faith of Rahab

points: Joshua rent his clothes and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark until the eventide, he and the elders of Israel, and put dust upon their heads, grieving over the war just lost and the men that died.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the Lord God of Israel, and make confession unto him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me. Joshua said hide it not from me because it was already not hidden from One mightier than he: we cannot hide what we do from the Lord.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua had said all the silver and gold and vessels were consecrated unto the Lord for his treasury, so Achan was not stealing from men; he was literally stealing from the Most High.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua sent messengers, and they ran unto the tent, and behold, it was hid in his tent, and the silver under it; they laid it all out before the Lord with the whole congregation present. The Lord revealed it, and the scripture cannot be broken: as Jericho was made a curse, so the one who took of it.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: Joshua took Achan with his sons, daughters, animals and tent to the valley of Achor, because the household had to have known and said nothing. Silence is agreement. Israel stoned and burned them and raised a heap of stones. Secret sin cost thirty-six men their lives and wiped out a whole family.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the garment, the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, asses, sheep, tent, and all that he had, unto the valley of Achor. His sons and daughters did not steal it, yet because he lacked knowledge and understanding they paid for the covetous spirit he carried.

note.label: Joshua 7: The Accursed Thing and the Sin of Achan

points: God told Joshua he had already given him Ai, yet commanded an ambush behind the city. The victory is ordained, but it must be won God's way.

note.label: War of the Gods

points: With the accursed thing purged, the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee and go up to Ai; see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour and sent them away by night to lie in ambush behind the city, not very far from it, always ready. These were warriors, men of courage, but none of that matters unless the spirit is right with the Lord first.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: The ambush went and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai, while Joshua lodged that night among the people; he rose early, numbered the people, and went up with the elders of Israel and pitched on the north side of Ai, with a valley between them and the city.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness: part of the strategy, feigning defeat so Ai would chase them straight into the ambush.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: The Lord said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Joshua drew not his hand back until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai, meaning the children were put to death also. This was not new: at Sihon's cities Israel utterly destroyed the men, the women, and the little ones. The children's song teaching that Christ loves all the children of every nation alike does not stand with these scriptures; the Lord's love is toward the children of Israel.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Only the cattle and the spoil of that city Israel took for a prey unto themselves, according unto the word of the Lord which he commanded Joshua: they carried out the order exactly as instructed.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: Joshua burnt Ai and made it an heap for ever, even a desolation unto this day; the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide, and as soon as the sun was down his carcase was taken down, cast at the entering of the gate of the city, and a great heap of stones raised thereon.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: There was not a word of all that Moses commanded which Joshua read not before all the congregation, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them: those were the strangers that fell in line with Israel, with the fear of the Lord in them, as Rahab had.

note.label: Joshua 8: The Taking of Ai and the Blessings and Cursings

points: When they heard what had been done, they gathered themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel with one accord.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal saying, We be come from a far country: now therefore make ye a league with us. Israel was commanded to destroy all the inhabitants of the land, the very nations listed in verse 1, so the Gibeonites' only hope was to pretend they were not of the land.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: Joshua called for them: wherefore have ye beguiled us, saying, We are very far from you, when ye dwell among us?

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: So did he unto them, and delivered them out of the hand of the children of Israel, that they slew them not; and Joshua made them that day hewers of wood and drawers of water for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, even unto this day.

note.label: Joshua 9: The Gibeonite Deception and the Weight of an Oath

points: Adoni-zedec king of Jerusalem heard how Joshua had taken Ai and utterly destroyed it. You might be confused why it says Jerusalem, since Jerusalem had not been set up as of yet because the land was not conquered: when the scribes wrote the history they left identifying location markers, so the reader knows visually where this is taking place.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at Gilgal: slack not thy hand from thy servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the mountains are gathered together against us.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The Lord said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. The Lord was always fighting for us and warring with the nations.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The LORD said unto Joshua, Fear them not: for I have delivered them into thine hand; there shall not a man of them stand before thee. So Joshua ascended from Gilgal all night with all the people of war and the mighty men of valour, and came unto them suddenly.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Joshua said in the sight of Israel, Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies. Time stopped. And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the Lord hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the Lord fought for Israel. The reason it stopped for him is his faith: he believed the Lord would do it.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Joshua spake to the LORD in the sight of Israel: Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. The sun stood still in the midst of heaven and hasted not to go down about a whole day, and there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man: for the LORD fought for Israel.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave, set men by it to keep them, and stay ye not: pursue after your enemies and smite the hindmost of them, for the LORD your God hath delivered them into your hand.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Then said Joshua, Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out those five kings unto me: the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The five kings fled and hid themselves in a cave at Makkedah, and Joshua said, Roll great stones upon the mouth of the cave; stay ye not, but pursue after your enemies. When they brought out those five kings, Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said unto the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. And Joshua said unto them, Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the Lord do to all your enemies against whom ye fight. This was Israel conquering the land of Canaan, and it is going to happen again in the future.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Joshua called for all the men of Israel and said to the captains of the men of war, Come near, put your feet upon the necks of these kings. Fear not, nor be dismayed, be strong and of good courage: for thus shall the LORD do to all your enemies against whom ye fight.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: They hid in caves, and that is what the nations are going to do again. What we read in Joshua is future prophecy: in the day of the Most High men shall go into the holes of the rocks and into the caves of the earth for fear of the LORD, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: Afterward Joshua smote them, slew them, and hanged them on five trees until the evening; at the going down of the sun they took them down, cast them into the cave wherein they had been hid, and laid great stones in the cave's mouth, which remain until this very day.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: That day Joshua took Makkedah and smote it with the edge of the sword; he utterly destroyed all the souls that were therein, he let none remain, and did to the king of Makkedah as he did unto the king of Jericho.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: The southern campaign rolled city by city: Libnah, then Lachish, which he took on the second day; Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua smote him and his people until he had left him none remaining.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: So Joshua smote all the country of the hills, of the south, of the vale, and of the springs, and all their kings; he left none remaining, but utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the LORD God of Israel commanded, from Kadesh-barnea even unto Gaza. All these kings did Joshua take at one time, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.

Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering: you could not gather enough wood or sacrifice enough animals to change his mind about the other nations. All nations before him are as nothing, and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity. All means all: no nation is excluded. No wonder the Most High gave Moses and Joshua the green light to destroy everything that breathed.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

points: And all these kings and their land did Joshua take at one time, because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The LORD said unto Joshua, Be not afraid because of them: for to morrow about this time will I deliver them up all slain before Israel: thou shalt hough their horses, and burn their chariots with fire.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: Joshua did unto them as the LORD bade him: he houghed their horses and burnt their chariots with fire.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: Joshua turned back and took Hazor, for Hazor beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms, and smote all the souls therein with the edge of the sword; there was not any left to breathe, and he burnt Hazor with fire. But as for the cities that stood still in their strength, Israel burned none of them, save Hazor only.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: Joshua took Hazor, which beforetime was the head of all those kingdoms, and utterly destroyed it, as Moses the servant of the Lord commanded. He left nothing undone of all that the Lord commanded Moses. Joshua made war a long time with all those kings; there was not a city that made peace with Israel save the Hivites: all other they took in battle.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: So Joshua took all that land, the hills, all the south country, all the land of Goshen, the valley, the plain, and the mountain of Israel; all their kings he took, and smote them, and slew them. Joshua made war a long time with all those kings.

We see the Most High setting it up right before our eyes: Israel is being made into warriors once again, so the days of Joshua can be once again when the Lord returns. He is setting us in order before our enemies' eyes.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: At that time came Joshua and cut off the Anakims from the mountains, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah and Israel; Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities. None of the Anakims were left in the land of the children of Israel: only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod there remained.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: So Joshua took the whole land, and gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: So Joshua took the whole land, according to all that the LORD said unto Moses, and gave it for an inheritance unto Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. And the land rested from war.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

points: These are the kings of the country which Joshua and the children of Israel smote on this side Jordan on the west, which Joshua gave unto the tribes of Israel for a possession according to their divisions: the kings of Jericho, Ai, Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, Eglon, Gezer, Debir, Geder, Hormah, Arad, Libnah, Adullam, Makkedah, Bethel, Tappuah, Hepher, Aphek, Lasharon, Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, Achshaph, Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Jokneam of Carmel, Dor, the nations of Gilgal, and Tirzah: all the kings thirty and one.

Joshua was a mighty man: thirty and one kings he took down in the power of the Most High. Let us now praise famous men and our fathers that begat us. In Ecclesiasticus he is called Jesus the son of Nave, for Joshua translated into the Greek is Jesus, and Nave is Nun: Joshua the son of Nun, valiant in the wars, the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God.

note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

points: Joshua is old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed. The Most High had already said he was not going to drive out these nations in one year, but little and little as Israel increased, so much land still remained.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

points: The countries in the land of Canaan were distributed by Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes, by lot, as the Most High commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes and the half tribe; Moses had already given the two tribes and a half their inheritance on the other side Jordan.

note.label: Joshua 14: Caleb Wholly Followed the Most High

points: Unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh was given a part among the children of Judah according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua: the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron. And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak.

note.label: Joshua 15: The Lot of the Tribe of Judah

points: They came near before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying the Lord commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their brethren; and according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The children of Joseph, led by Ephraim, asked Joshua why he gave them but one lot to inherit, seeing they are a great people; great here means numerous. Ephraim and Manasseh were among the most populated tribes, and Ephraim's own portion had already been given back in chapter 16.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: Joshua answered without bias: if thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, into the forest, and cut down there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee. Narrow means too small: if you are complaining that your lot is too small, then go to war and conquer more land.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

points: The men arose and passed through the land and described it by cities into seven parts in a book, and came again to Joshua to the host at Shiloh.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

points: Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the Lord, and there divided the land unto the children of Israel according to their divisions; Shiloh, where the lots were cast, sat in the land of Ephraim.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

points: Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes divided the inheritances by lot in Shiloh before the Lord, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country; everybody had their portion, and everyone was satisfied.

note.label: Joshua 19: The Portions of the Remaining Tribes

points: The heads of the fathers of the Levites came near to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua, and to the heads of the tribes at Shiloh, because the tribe of Levi had been appointed cities to dwell in with suburbs for their cattle, and the time had come to receive them.

note.label: Joshua 21: The Cities of the Levites

points: A long time after the Most High had given rest unto Israel from all their enemies round about, Joshua waxed old and stricken in age, and he called for all Israel, their elders, heads, judges, and officers to give his last charge.

note.label: Joshua 23: Cleave unto the Lord Your God

points: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, with the elders, heads, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God for the covenant.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua said unto the people, Ye cannot serve the LORD: for he is an holy God; he is a jealous God; he will not forgive your transgressions nor your sins.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: The people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the LORD. It is the same thing Israel told Moses back then; we came into that covenant again, this time without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua said, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him; and they said, We are witnesses. Everybody was in full agreement.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem, the same thing Moses his predecessor did at the mountain; Joshua was his successor and did the same, though without the blood.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up under an oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: So Joshua let the people depart, every man unto his inheritance.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: After these things Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being an hundred and ten years old.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua, which had known all the works of the LORD that he had done for Israel.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: After the death of Joshua the children of Israel ask the Most High who shall go up first against the Canaanites, and the answer is Judah: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.

note.label: Judges 1: Judah Goes Up First, but the Inhabitants Are Not Driven Out

points: The people served the Most High all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great works he did for Israel.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: Because this people transgressed the covenant and did not hearken, the Most High declares he will not henceforth drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: if ye cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty the Most High will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

points: In his days Hiel of Bethel rebuilds Jericho, laying its foundation in his firstborn Abiram and setting up its gates in his youngest Segub, according to the word spoken by Joshua.

note.label: 1 Kings 16: Baasha to Ahab and the Rise of Baal Worship

points: For if Jesus had given them rest: that Jesus is Joshua. Joshua was mighty and smote the nations of Canaan, but there were enemies on every side, so the land was not the true rest. There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God: the seventh day Sabbath is the similitude, and the substance is the kingdom, reigning with Christ.
